transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

I’m here because something’s been going on at work for months. I’m an interpreter and translator, and I keep seeing the same pattern in our project files. Certain subcontractors, and one colleague in particular, are making these tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed.

IT keeps saying the audit trail is clean, but I don’t buy that. The record has been arranged in a way that puts the blame on me, and I need someone to understand what’s happening.
Over these past few months, have you also noticed periods where your mood, energy, or self-confidence felt unusually high or elevated, beyond just being worried about this situation at work?

No, I don’t think so. I’ve been stressed and more alert because of what’s happening at work, but I wouldn’t say my mood or confidence has been unusually high. It’s more concern and frustration than anything elevated.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds, or seen things, that other people around you didn't seem to hear or see?
No, I haven’t had anything like that. I mean, I’ve been paying close attention to things, especially at work, but I’m not hearing voices or seeing things that other people don’t.

Aside from this situation at work, have you generally found yourself distrustful or suspicious of other people's motives in your personal relationships or in other areas of your life, going back to when you were younger?

No, not generally. I mean, I’m not someone who goes around thinking everyone has bad motives. I get along with my family, keep up with things at home, pay bills, manage my team’s workflow, still do my translation work.

It’s really this project issue—when the file history comes up, or certain coworkers are involved, that’s where things go off track for me. Outside of that, I wouldn’t say I’ve been suspicious of people my whole life.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre delusional belief (that coworkers are tampering with files to sabotage him) persisting for months, in the absence of hallucinations, mood episode symptoms, or broader pervasive suspiciousness characteristic of a personality disorder. Functioning is preserved outside the delusional theme (maintains work performance, family relationships, daily responsibilities), which argues against schizophrenia (no other psychotic domains, no functional decline) and against paranoid personality disorder (suspicion is circumscribed to the specific situation rather than lifelong and pervasive). This pattern—an encapsulated, persistent delusion without other psychotic or mood symptoms and with intact psychosocial functioning—is most consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22).
